answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and scoped to the primary region during settlement peak, so the leading fit is shifting writes off that region rather than shedding them. memory_b2 is the closest prior: regional failover restored latency in minutes without dropping traffic. Rollback (memory_b1) remains a live alternative because a release shipped two hours ago, but a globally applied build would not usually present as single-region write latency, and rolling back mid-settlement is a second-order risk until the archive is checked. Circuit breaking would fail customer writes, contradicting the objective; read-replica routing addressed dashboard reads, not this write path; pre-peak capacity add is the wrong shape for an already-concentrated regional degradation. Verify b2 and b1 before committing; treat failover as reversible and watch settlement/downstream completeness.
